title: The Shortcut I Didn't Take
scene: Walking to the station on a sunny morning, the narrator chooses the familiar route over a map's shortcut, notices a habit of checking the time, and sees a dog refusing to cross a puddle.
sceneJa: 駅へ向かう朝、地図アプリが近道を示す。時間に余裕があるので公園沿いの道を選ぶが、つい何度も時刻を確認してしまう。スマホをしまうと、水たまりを断固として避ける犬が目に入る。

chunks.en: On my way to the station,

chunks.ja: 地図アプリが近道を示した

chunks.en: I was tempted to try it,
chunks.ja: 試してみたくなったが、

chunks.en: was already bright with morning sun.
chunks.ja: もう朝日で明るくなっていた。

chunks.en: I had ten minutes to spare,
so I took the longer route past the park.
chunks.ja: 公園の横を通る遠回りの道を選んだ。

chunks.en: I caught myself checking the time
chunks.ja: また時刻を確認している自分に気づいた

chunks.en: even though I wasn't running late.
chunks.ja: 遅れそうでもないのに。

chunks.en: I slipped my phone into my pocket
chunks.ja: スマホをポケットにしまうと、

chunks.en: stubbornly refusing to cross a puddle.
chunks.ja: 水たまりをどうしても渡ろうとしない犬だ。

chunks.en: By the time I reached the station,

chunks.ja: まだ時間に余裕があって、

chunks.en: and I was still smiling about that dog.
chunks.ja: あの犬のことを思い出して、まだ笑っていた。

questions.question: Which split keeps the self-observation expression together?
options: I caught / myself checking the time / even though I wasn't running late.
I caught myself checking the time / even though I wasn't running late.
I caught myself / checking the time even / though I wasn't running late.
questions.explanation: 'I caught myself + -ing' means noticing yourself doing something automatically. Keep it together as a meaningful unit.

questions.question: What does 'I had ten minutes to spare' mean?
options: I had ten extra minutes before I needed to arrive.
I was already ten minutes late.
I had to wait exactly ten minutes for the map.
questions.explanation: 'Time to spare' means extra time available beyond what is needed.

questions.question: Why does the narrator put the phone away?
options: To save battery for an urgent call.
To hide the map from someone.
To stop unnecessary time-checking and pay attention to the walk.
questions.explanation: The narrator notices the time-checking habit despite having time to spare, and shifts attention to the surroundings.

speak: Imagine: you are walking somewhere with more time than usual. Read: follow the choice between the shortcut and the familiar route. Chunk: practice 'I was tempted to ...', 'I had ... to spare', and 'I caught myself ...-ing' as units. Understand: temptation, available time, and noticing an automatic habit are different meanings. Check: answer three questions. Speak (30 seconds): describe a tempting shortcut, how much time you had to spare, and one thing you caught yourself doing. Reuse 'On second thought ...' to change your decision. Final Read: read all six sentences aloud; pause after 'On second thought', stress 'ten minutes to spare', and soften your tone for the dog at the end.
review: New: 'I was tempted to ...'（〜したくなった）, 'I had ... to spare'（〜だけ余裕があった）, 'I caught myself ...-ing'（無意識に〜している自分に気づいた）. Reuse 'On second thought' (Lessons 115/120) for a walking-route decision and 'By the time ...' (Lessons 112/118) for arrival without a rush. Unlike Lessons 107–120, this is not a task finished or a mistake fixed, but a small shift of attention. Fictional story. Sources: https://www.oxfordlearnersdictionaries.com/definition/american_english/tempt ; https://dictionary.cambridge.org/us/dictionary/english/spare
